ops.title: hook gate misreports load-induced handshake timeouts as 'signed host is not installed and ready'
ops.description:
The session gate classifies ANY wire handshake failure — including raw-read/ack timeouts against a healthy, serving host under machine load — as not-installed, and prescribes `capt-hook helper install` (itself a no-op wrapper: 0ef22da).

Field evidence 2026-07-27 (local, fully converged 12.20.12, host 81227): load 64–86 during an 11-lane release wave → every new session flagged "Failed with non-blocking status code: captain: signed host is not installed and ready; run `capt-hook helper install`: wire: handshake failed: read acknowledge: wire: wait for frame: raw-read unix ->…", while `capt-hook helper status` RPCs reached the host fine. Server side showed the matching dead-peer race: SecCodeCopyGuestWithAttributes OSStatus 100003 (ESRCH) flood — daemonkit bug 6215482. Mechanism: client's short ack deadline expires while the loaded host is still verifying the peer; client dies; host then finds no such process.

Wrong remedy pointer: a user following it would reinstall a healthy deployment. Fix direction: distinguish timeout/slow-host (transient — say so, retry with backoff or lengthen/adapt the probe deadline) from absent/unsigned host (which alone should carry the install pointer).

ops.text: The gate's user-facing message distinguishes a handshake timeout against a live socket from a missing/unready installation; only the latter prescribes install
A probe timeout under machine load does not surface the install remedy pointer
